title: AI service data usage and reverse engineering clause (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This draft clause is designed as an exhibit to the Master Services Agreement (MSA) or Data Processing Agreement (DPA) to address explicit limits and obligations relating to (1) customer data usage for model improvement or retraining, (2) prohibitions on reverse engineering of customer integrations and outputs, and (3) technical and operational safeguards that evidence compliance. The language below is intentionally prescriptive but flaggable for negotiation points.

Scope and definitions (for this exhibit):
- "Customer Data": any data, content, prompts, responses, embeddings, or metadata submitted by Customer to Provider under the Agreement.
- "Derived Models": any model weights, parameter updates, or derivative models created by Provider using Customer Data.
- "Proprietary Components": Provider code, model architectures, weights, prompting templates, and internal optimizations not provided to Customer.
- "Reverse Engineering": attempting to reconstruct Provider’s Proprietary Components, backend logic, model weights, or training data from API responses, model outputs, or observed behavior.

1) Permitted uses of Customer Data
1.1 Operational processing: Provider may process Customer Data to provide the services as described in the Agreement (request handling, streaming responses, embeddings, logging for debugging, billing).
1.2 Limited service improvement with Customer consent: Provider shall not use Customer Data to improve, fine-tune, or train models (including Derived Models) except where Customer has given explicit, written consent (e.g., a checked box in an onboarding flow and a signed amendment). Such consent shall be revocable upon reasonable notice and shall be scoped to the specific project, time period, and datasets identified.
1.3 Aggregation and de-identification: Provider may use aggregated and de-identified telemetry that cannot reasonably be re-associated to Customer or an individual (per Provider’s de-identification policy) for product improvement and monitoring. Aggregated telemetry excludes raw prompts, embeddings, and outputs tied to unique identifiers retained by Provider.

2) Prohibition on reverse engineering and model reconstruction
2.1 Customer obligations: Customer shall not attempt to reverse engineer, reconstruct, or extract Provider Proprietary Components, model weights, or training datasets from the services. This includes but is not limited to: parameter extraction attacks, membership inference attempts, model inversion, prompt mining at scale, and other systematic probing to recreate model behavior.
2.2 Technical enforcement and monitoring: Provider may implement reasonable technical controls to detect and throttle behavior indicative of model extraction (e.g., high-rate synthetic probing, repeated high-entropy gradient estimates). Provider will notify Customer if their integration is observed to be the source of such probing and may temporarily rate-limit traffic consistent with the Agreement and operational SLOs.
2.3 Remedies: Breach of this section is a material breach. In addition to other remedies, Provider may suspend service, require remediation steps, invoice for investigations, and seek injunctive relief.

3) Use of outputs and downstream rights
3.1 Customer outputs: Customer is granted a license to use model outputs provided by the service for its business purposes, including redistribution to end-users, subject to applicable law and the Agreement. 
3.2 No implicit license to Proprietary Components: Customer’s right to outputs does not include any right to obtain, recreate, or claim ownership over Provider model weights, training methods, or internal optimization techniques.

4) Data provenance and evidence obligations
4.1 Audit evidence: On reasonable request and subject to confidentiality and security considerations, Provider will provide Customer with a description of processing activities relevant to the Customer’s data (ingest, retention windows, data flows, and types of telemetry collected). Requests requiring logs or samples tied to specific requests will require a mutually agreed process and may be subject to redaction to protect other customers and Proprietary Components.
4.2 Third-party audits: For enterprise customers with an executed SOC2/PCI/GDPR annex, Provider will reasonably cooperate with auditor access to evidence related only to Customer’s processing (e.g., KMS key rotation records, access logs for Customer tenant, export of audit trail for given time window). Provider may provide redacted artifacts that preserve other customers’ confidentiality.

5) Security and operational controls (implementation notes)
5.1 Data segregation: Provider will isolate Customer Data logically and, where applicable, physically (Dedicated or Private deployments) to enforce data residency and isolation commitments in the Agreement.
5.2 Key management: For Private and Dedicated customers electing customer-managed keys, Provider will support KMS/HSM integration and will log key usage events.
5.3 Logging and retention: Provider will retain request/response logs only for the retention period agreed in the Agreement or DPA. Default retention for troubleshooting telemetry is 30 days unless extended by contract.
5.4 Access controls: Provider will enforce least-privilege access for personnel, MFA for operator consoles, and role-based access controls to production and audit logs.
5.5 Detection and response: Provider will maintain detection capabilities for model-extraction patterns and will publish a runbook for incident response tied to such events for enterprise customers under NDA.

6) Liability, indemnities, and limits
6.1 Indemnity carve-out for reverse engineering: Provider accepts liability for damages resulting from Provider’s unauthorized use of Customer Data in violation of Section 1.2. Customer is responsible for damages resulting from Customer’s breach of the reverse-engineering prohibition.
6.2 Limitation of damages: To the extent permitted by law, both parties’ liability for claims arising exclusively from reverse engineering or model-extraction remediation shall be capped at the amounts set forth in the MSA, except where willful misconduct or gross negligence is proven.

7) Negotiation points (commonly requested by counterparties)
- Customer requests to allow opt-out of aggregated telemetry collection: operationally feasible, but requires clear UI and backfill considerations.
- Requests for longer log retention for specific regulatory needs: possible in Dedicated/Private, requires pricing and SRE operational changes.
- Requests to allow limited research use of outputs for benchmarking: acceptable if mutually agreed scope, timebox, and no attempt to derive Proprietary Components.

8) Implementation checklist for commercial teams (operational items to include in SOW/Order Form)
- Whether Customer consents to training/fine-tuning (yes/no) and scope of consent.
- Retention windows for logs and telemetry specific to this Customer.
- Deployment mode: Hosted | Dedicated | Private. (Dedicated/Private may permit more permissive data uses with pricing adjustments.)
- KMS/HSM requirements and who manages keys.
- SLA thresholds for detection/notification of suspected extraction attempts.
- Audit rights and frequency (annual, on-demand with notice).

9) Sample redlines (for legal teams)
- "Provider shall not use Customer Data to improve models" -> Add option: "unless Customer opts in via Section X and receives documented protections and data-handling procedures".
- "Customer shall not attempt to reverse engineer" -> Add mutual obligation: "Both parties shall refrain from activities that seek to reconstruct the other party’s Proprietary Components from outputs or telemetry" for stronger reciprocity in partner integrations.

10) Notes and rationale for product/ops
- Detection and throttling: Product should define thresholds (requests/day, repeated high-entropy prompts, token-extraction heuristics) and a mitigation playbook (warn -> throttle -> suspend).
- De-identification rubric: Product and legal should agree on an operational definition of "de-identified" that maps to code paths that remove unique identifiers before aggregation.
- Evidence requests: Build a secure automated export for tenant-scoped audit trails to reduce time and cost of ad-hoc investigations.

Document status: draft for review by Security & Compliance, Product Legal, and Sales Operations.
Open questions:
- Should revocation of training consent include a destructive wipe of previously derived model checkpoints? (ops: technically complex; legal: desirable for some customers)
- Minimum evidence standard for proving a suspected extraction came from a specific Customer (is IP forensic possible for high-noise environments?).

Revision history:
- 2025-11-12: initial draft (Aisha Patel)
- 2026-01-18: added audit and KMS sections (Rina Kapoor)
- 2026-03-01: revised liability carve-outs and implementation checklist (Diego Martinez)

Negotiation guidance (one-liners for AE/CS):
- If customer asks for training rights: accept only with explicit opt-in, clear timebox, and pricing; require Dedicated/Private for longer retention or broader uses.
- If customer requests unlimited log access: push back with redacted exports and scoped auditor access; charge for bespoke log retention.
- If customer demands reverse-engineering carve-in: decline or require reciprocal restrictions and very narrow scope.

End of exhibit.
